sourceAtom.visibleSubtitle: Construct a cumulative frequency histogram and ogive

inlines.latex: \begin{align*}\text{c.c.}&=\tfrac{10+14}{2},\ \tfrac{15+19}{2},\ \tfrac{20+24}{2},\ \tfrac{25+29}{2}=12,\ 17,\ 22,\ 27\\\text{c.f.}&=3,\ 3+6,\ 9+4,\ 13+2=3,\ 9,\ 13,\ 15\\\Sigma f&=15\\\text{Bars}&:\text{touching, centred at }12,17,22,27\text{ with heights }3,9,13,15\\\text{Ogive}&:\text{start at the left edge of the first bar at height }0\text{, then join each upper-right corner}\end{align*}

inlines.text: frequency histogram and ogive for each table.

answer.short:
Class	c.c.	$f$	c.f.
20–24	$22$	$5$	$5$
25–29	$27$	$2$	$7$
30–34	$32$	$6$	$13$
35–39	$37$	$3$	$16$

$\Sigma f=16$. Bars of heights $5,7,13,16$ centred at $22,27,32,37$; ogive from the left edge of the first bar at height $0$ through $(1,5),(2,7),(3,13),(4,16)$ in class widths.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{c.c.}&=\tfrac{20+24}{2},\ \tfrac{25+29}{2},\ \tfrac{30+34}{2},\ \tfrac{35+39}{2}=22,\ 27,\ 32,\ 37\\\text{c.f.}&=5,\ 5+2,\ 7+6,\ 13+3=5,\ 7,\ 13,\ 16\\\Sigma f&=16\end{align*}$$
Draw touching bars centred at $22,27,32,37$ with heights $5,7,13,16$. Start the ogive at the left edge of the first bar on the baseline, then join the upper-right bar corners.

answer.short:
Class	c.c.	$f$	c.f.
0–9	$4.5$	$2$	$2$
10–19	$14.5$	$0$	$2$
20–29	$24.5$	$5$	$7$
30–39	$34.5$	$3$	$10$

$\Sigma f=10$. Bars of heights $2,2,7,10$ centred at $4.5,14.5,24.5,34.5$; ogive from the left edge of the first bar at height $0$ through $(1,2),(2,2),(3,7),(4,10)$ in class widths.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{c.c.}&=\tfrac{0+9}{2},\ \tfrac{10+19}{2},\ \tfrac{20+29}{2},\ \tfrac{30+39}{2}=4.5,\ 14.5,\ 24.5,\ 34.5\\\text{c.f.}&=2,\ 2+0,\ 2+5,\ 7+3=2,\ 2,\ 7,\ 10\\\Sigma f&=10\end{align*}$$
Draw touching bars centred on the class centres with heights $2,2,7,10$. Start the ogive at the left edge of the first bar on the baseline, then join the upper-right corners. It is horizontal across class $10$–$19$ because its frequency is $0$.

sourceAtom.label: Example
sourceAtom.visibleSubtitle: Find the interquartile range from an ogive

inlines.text: Determine the IQR from this ogive.
From each position, read horizontally to the ogive, then down to the score axis.

content.prompt: Determine the IQR from these ogives.

answer.worked:
Total frequency: $60$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Lower quartile position}&=0.25\times60=15\\\text{Upper quartile position}&=0.75\times60=45\end{align*}$$
Read horizontally to the ogive, then down to the score axis: $Q_1\approx35$ and $Q_3\approx55$.
$$\mathrm{IQR}\approx55-35=20.$$

Total frequency: $50$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Lower quartile position}&=0.25\times50=12.5\\\text{Upper quartile position}&=0.75\times50=37.5\end{align*}$$
Read horizontally to the ogive, then down to the score axis: $Q_1\approx25$ and $Q_3\approx55$.
$$\mathrm{IQR}\approx55-25=30.$$

content.prompt: In a survey of 40 students, 14 catch the bus to school.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What fraction of the students catch the bus? Give your answer in simplest form.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What percentage of the students catch the bus?

payloads.replacement:
To spot patterns in many numerical values, we group them into intervals called **classes**. Each value belongs to exactly one class, so the classes have no gaps and no overlaps.

Grouping data can reveal trends, but individual data values are lost.

Here are the raw times (in seconds) for 25 students completing a 400 m race:

63.2, 71.8, 58.4, 66.1, 74.3, 61.7, 69.5, 57.9, 72.6, 64.8, 78.2, 60.3, 67.4,
55.6, 73.1, 62.9, 68.7, 76.4, 59.1, 65.3, 70.8, 56.2, 63.7, 71.2, 66.9

For **continuous** data (data that can take any value in an interval, such as a time), write the classes as inequalities. The first class has been set up for you.

Histograms of grouped data have frequency on the $y$-axis and **class centre** on the $x$-axis.

The class centre of a class is the midpoint of its lower and upper ends: $\dfrac{\text{lower end}+\text{upper end}}{2}$.

Grouping loses the individual data values, so a mean or median from grouped data is an **estimate**.

To estimate the mean, use the class centre of each class in place of its data values.

1. Find the class centres.
2. Multiply each class centre by its frequency: $cc\times f$.
3. Divide the sum of the $cc\times f$ values by the total frequency: $\overline{x}=\frac{\Sigma(cc\times f)}{\Sigma f}$

Estimate the median using an **ogive** (cumulative frequency line).

Find the median position: 50% of the total cumulative frequency.

Draw a horizontal line from the median position to the ogive.

Read off the $x$-value below that point. For grouped data, this value is an estimate.
